## ascend

Blocks **1** card.

- **(engine)** The static `condition` tree itself has SHIPPED (see `tests/unit/test_static_condition.py`): a static may now carry `all`/`any`/`not`/`exists`/`is_your_turn`/`cmp` over `{"const": n}` and `{"count": filter}`, and the count filter may name a zone. What is still missing for this card is a *leaf* for that tree to read, and it is the leaf named below, not the tree. For this card that leaf is the blessing itself: part (d) of the work below is a condition leaf -- e.g. `{"has_city_s_blessing": "you"}` -- so the second printed line can be `{"kind": "static", "effect": "grant_keyword", "affects": {"self_only": true}, "keywords": ["flying"], "condition": {...}}`. It belongs to this capability rather than to a separate one: a player-state flag and the way to read it are one piece of work, and the blessing is a pipeline input (player state, not a derived characteristic) so it is safe in the condition language exactly as a zone count is. the city's blessing as a per-player, one-way, permanent designation (rule 702.131 / 700.6): a field on `PlayerState` such as `has_city_s_blessing: bool`, set the moment its controller controls ten or more permanents and never unset -- it survives the permanents leaving, survives the source of the Ascend ability leaving the battlefield, and is shared by every card that player controls, so a second Ascend card printed later reads the blessing that a first card granted. Needs three parts: (a) the player-state field itself; (b) the continuous check, which is a STATE TRIGGER, not a triggered ability -- it is checked whenever state-based actions are, uses no stack and cannot be responded to, so it belongs in the state-based-action pass in `engine/` next to the existing legend-rule/lethal-damage checks, gated on the controller of a permanent (or resolving spell) with the Ascend ability; and (c) card-level vocabulary to say the permanent has Ascend at all -- most plausibly a card field like `"ascend": true`, since it is a one-word keyword ability with no parameters, and since making it a `Keyword` enum member would wrongly put it in the derived keyword list that `grant_keyword` and evasion checks read
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `PlayerState` (`src/automtg/engine/player.py:20-65`) stores life, zones, mana, land drops, commander tax/damage, loss and UI flags -- there is no general per-player flag, designation or counter of any kind, so the blessing has nowhere to live and no value expression or condition can read it back. The closest one-way flag in the engine is `monstrous` (`engine/objects.py:46-48`, set by the `monstrosity` op at `effects/ops_board.py:252`), and it is wrong in all three respects that matter here: it lives on an OBJECT, so it is cleared by `reset_permanent_state` on any zone change and cannot be shared between two cards; it is set by an op resolving from the stack rather than by a continuous check; and there is no op-driven route to a player-wide equivalent, because none of the 46 ops writes durable player state. Nor can a triggered ability substitute. The `if` op's condition language CAN count permanents -- `{"cmp": ">=", "left": {"count": {"controller": "you"}}, "right": {"const": 10}}` is well-formed -- but every available trigger event fires on a discrete happening (`self_enters`, `permanent_enters`, `upkeep`, ...), and Ascend is not an event: a player who is at nine permanents when this creature enters and reaches ten by playing a land gets the blessing at the instant of the tenth, with no trigger of this card's having fired, and gets it during an opponent's turn just as readily. A trigger-plus-counter version would also be a DIFFERENT card in the direction that matters, since the blessing is never lost and a re-checked trigger would come and go. The seven player-wide statics (`effect: "extra_land_drops"`, `no_hand_limit`, `play_lands_from_graveyard`, `play_lands_from_library_top`, `double_land_triggers`, `double_land_mana`, `freeze_opponent_lands`, `docs/card-dsl.md` "Player-wide statics") are the only things in the DSL that describe a player rather than a characteristic, and each is an unconditional permission read live off the battlefield for as long as its source is there -- none of them SETS anything, and all of them stop when the source leaves, which is the opposite of "for the rest of the game"

## cards-drawn-this-turn

Blocks **1** card.

- **(value)** a per-turn tally of how many cards a player has drawn, readable as a value expression -- e.g. `{"cards_drawn_this_turn": "you"}` -- reset during cleanup, and incremented by every draw whatever caused it (draw step, spell, ability, or a replacement that draws). Kydele spells it `{"op": "add_mana", "mana": "{C}", "amount": {"cards_drawn_this_turn": "you"}}` and needs nothing else, because the variable mana ability machinery it plugs into already ships.
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `VALUE_KEYS` has no event tally of any kind. `count` walks a zone and counts objects, so the closest spelling -- counting the hand -- is a different number the moment anything is played, discarded or drawn on an opponent's turn. `cards_in_hand` has the same problem for the same reason. Nothing on `PlayerState` records draws: the fields are life, zones, mana, land drops, commander tax/damage, loss and UI flags, and none of them is a per-turn counter. The `draw` EventType exists and is emitted, so the tally has a natural place to be incremented, but no state to be incremented into and no cleanup hook resetting it. This is the same shape of missing bookkeeping as `damaged-by-source-this-turn` -- a per-turn ledger keyed by player rather than by object -- and whichever ships first should decide where per-turn counters live.

Kydele is the one it does not reach, and for a different reason: its multiplier is not a board count. `{"count": <selector>}` counts objects, and "cards you've drawn this turn" is a per-turn tally of an *event*, which the engine does not keep.
